claims.text: The starting material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated starting alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and is brittle.
The proposed intervention is introduction of a metastable high-entropy dual-phase alloy composition.
Metastable high-entropy dual-phase alloys can overcome a strength-ductility trade-off.
Applying the metastable dual-phase composition to the stated eutectic alloy will improve its tensile ductility.
Applying the metastable dual-phase composition to the stated eutectic alloy will retain or increase its tensile strength.
The structural mediator of the intervention is a hierarchy of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Dislocation glide controls deformation under the proposed room-temperature tensile conditions.
Twinning controls deformation under the proposed room-temperature tensile conditions.
The claimed improvement applies at room temperature under uniaxial tension.
The comparison baseline is the eutectic alloy without the metastable dual-phase composition.
The exact composition and processing conditions needed to obtain the desired properties are uncertain.
The proposed falsification experiment compares treated and untreated eutectic alloys using uniaxial tensile tests.
The falsification experiment will measure tensile strength, tensile ductility, and microstructure.
The hypothesis is falsified if the intervention does not improve both tensile ductility and strength.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis presents the hierarchical dual-phase lamellar structure as something introduced, while the initial state already contains that same structure and the intervention field specifies only a compositional change. No intervention-induced structural change is defined.

The main hypothesis permits strength to be merely retained, whereas the predicted outcome and falsification rule require strength to improve. An intervention that improves ductility while retaining unchanged strength would satisfy the main hypothesis but be classified as falsifying it by the stated rule.
